title: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
summary: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, now Bodrum in Turkey, was a monumental tomb for Maussollos, satrap of Karia, who died in 353 BC. A podium carried an Ionic colonnade, a 24-step pyramid and a chariot group, about 42 m high per Pliny. Little was visible when Hospitallers arrived in 1407, and they dismantled the remains in 1522.

uncertainty.note: Getty CONA: construction began ca. 367 BCE; World History Encyclopedia: c. 367 to 350 BCE; Cambridge: no exact start or end given, sculptures c. 350 BC. End is the 1522 dismantling recorded by the Cambridge chapter; the collapse date is unknown.

reviewer_note: Destroyed monument; model is a reconstruction from ancient-source and excavation figures. Shape choice: stepped_pyramid (podium plus 24-step pyramid; no closer shape exists, so the silhouette is approximate). Height about 42 m is Pliny's 140 ft as reported by the Cambridge chapter (Getty gives 43 m; WHE 45 m). Podium 38 x 32 m is from WHE; Livius (not cited) reads the substructure as 32 x 26 m. Least sure: height, and the date of collapse (unknown; possibly earthquake).

footprint.description: Podium of 38 x 32 m per modern excavation as summarised by World History Encyclopedia; Newton excavated the site in 1856–1857 and Danish excavations followed in 1966–1977 (Cambridge). No survey polygon opened.

phases.description: Built c. 367 to 350 BCE for Maussollos (died 353 BC).
Stood for several centuries; the date of its collapse is unknown.
Little visible when Hospitaller crusaders arrived in 1407; they quarried the ruins for their castle.
Remains dismantled in 1522; only foundations and fragments recovered by later excavation.
